Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to John Smith, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are David Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Alex Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Operating Officer; Robert Hayes, VP of Exploration; Lisa Chen, VP of Marketing; Elena Vasquez, Chief Sustainability Officer; and Mike Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to David Thompson.

David Thompson: Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved record production volumes averaging 248,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, up 3.3% quarter-over-quarter and 12.7% year-over-year, with oil volumes hitting 182,000 barrels per day. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on realized pricing, where hedging programs added significant value—our oil realizations averaged $76.45 per barrel and gas $3.12 per MCF, bolstered by $50 million in hedging gains. We are focused on our midstream segment's record transportation volumes of 4.2 million barrels of oil equivalent per day. Further, we are working on capital allocation priorities, including a 12% dividend increase to $0.55 per share quarterly and aggressive share repurchases. We continue to adjust to ESG initiatives, achieving a 22% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions year-to-date. We are advancing production growth in key basins like the Permian. We are evaluating environmental performance with minimal spills and proactive remediation. Finally, we are taking steps to optimize capital expenditures and maintain a strong balance sheet with net debt at 0.8 times EBITDA.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, David. As David mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.5 billion, up 15% year-over-year. Operating income was $800 million, and net income was $500 million. We generated $1.2 billion in free cash flow and returned $600 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $4.2 billion in total debt, $1.35 billion in cash, and net debt of $2.85 billion.

Let me dive deeper into some key areas. First, on realized prices and the impact of our hedging programs. This quarter, we realized strong pricing overall, supported by robust global demand and our disciplined hedging strategy, which shielded us from volatility in crude and gas markets.

For crude oil, our realized price averaged $76.45 per barrel, up 8% sequentially from Q2 and 12% year-over-year. This was favorable to the NYMEX WTI benchmark averaging $81.25 per barrel, with a $4.80 per barrel discount reflecting our blended basket—65% from Permian Basin production realizing a $1.20 per barrel basis to WTI due to better takeaway from Enterprise Midstream expansions and our Crestwood Waha plant optimizations. In Eagle Ford, basis tightened to -$0.85 per barrel versus WTI on stronger LLS differentials from Gulf Coast refinery runs.

Hedging was key: 65% of Q2 oil production was covered under swaps and collars with a $72.50 floor and $85.00 cap, generating a $2.15 per barrel positive impact or $28 million in cash flow. Unhedged, it would have been $74.30 per barrel, hit by mid-quarter WTI dips below $78 on OPEC+ signals and EIA inventory builds. Collars allowed $3.20 per barrel upside capture during late-June rallies to $84 on driving season and Middle East concerns. We've rolled forward swaps at $75-78 per barrel for H2 2024 on 50% of volumes, guarding against non-OPEC growth in Guyana and Brazil.

For natural gas, realizations averaged $3.12 per MCF, up 15% from Q2 but flat year-over-year amid oversupply. This was $0.38 below Henry Hub's $3.50 average, due to basis in key plays. Haynesville (55% of gas) saw -$0.65 per MCF basis from pipeline constraints on Haynesville Global amid LNG ramps at Plaquemines and Corpus Christi. Permian gas (30%) realized -$1.10 per MCF at Waha from flaring cuts and DCP Midstream expansions.

Hedging covered 75% with fixed swaps at $3.25 per MCF (45%) and collars at $2.80 floor/$4.20 cap (30%), delivering $0.45 per MCF uplift or $22 million in gains, boosting adjusted EBITDAX by 7%. Unhedged would have been $2.67 per MCF amid spot drops to $2.90 on weather and storage. Basis swaps added $0.12 per MCF in Haynesville protection. For Q4, 60% coverage at $3.10 swaps, 45% for 2025 at $3.40, eyeing LNG from Golden Pass and Freeport restarts compressing differentials.

Overall, hedging contributed $50 million to FCF, 22% of total before working capital, vital amid Brent-WTI spreads at $4.50 and gas production records at 104 Bcf/d. Full-year, expect oil $74-78 per barrel, gas $2.90-3.30 per MCF at WTI $78-85 and Henry Hub $3.20-3.60, with 55-65% hedged.

Our approach targets 50-70% hedging on 12-24 month production to de-risk DD&A and support $1.2 billion base dividend plus $500 million buybacks. We avoid over-hedging for upside—85% captured in Q3 rallies. Our in-house desk with AI decline curves improved layering 15% YoY. Monitoring OPEC+ into 2025 for WTI over $80, U.S. gas on winter exports amid Russian curbs.

Now, turning to our midstream segment performance, a cornerstone delivering stable fee-based cash flows. Assets transported a record 4.2 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, up 7% year-over-year and 3% sequentially. 92% volumes backed by take-or-pay or MVCs, insulating from WTI swings $75-87.

Crude volumes averaged 2.1 million barrels per day, up 9% YoY—highest ever. Permian Longhorn Pipeline hit 850,000 barrels per day, up 12%, on 6.2 million barrels per day basin output despite $2.50 Waha discounts. Bakken Dakota Access integration to 450,000 barrels per day on flaring cuts. Gulf Coast exports steady 650,000 barrels per day supporting 4.1 million barrels per day U.S. exports to Asia.

Natural gas at 4.2 Bcf per day, up 5% sequentially on heating and LNG. Haynesville Connector JV at 95% utilization to Gulf LNG through 2028. Marcellus 1.1 Bcf per day, 85% contracted despite $2.10 Dominion South pricing.

NGLs at 520,000 barrels per day, up 14%, on ethane rejection reversals; Mont Belvieu fractionation 480,000 barrels per day yielded $45 million spreads, up 20%, with exports over 1.2 million barrels per day.

Revenues up 11% to $1.2 billion, EBITDA up 15% to $850 million, 71% margin. Tariffs $0.85 per barrel crude, $0.12/Dth gas.

Infrastructure: $2.8 billion 2024 capex. Placed Permian Highway expansion (300 MMcf/d, $180 million under budget, 98% utilization, 15% IRR); NGL Header upgrade (100,000 barrels per day, $150 million); Eagle Ford Connector 75% complete ($400 million, Q4 online, 85% take-or-pay).

Digital: AI analytics on 2,500 pipeline miles cut integrity digs 30%; drones 25% vegetation savings; DAS detected 15 leak precursors, 99.98% reliability.

Permian 55% EBITDA, Gulf Coast 25% on Europe LNG surge. Exploring Appalachia JV. Guidance $3.2 billion distributable cash flow at 12x multiple. 5-8% volume growth to 2027, 50% FCF returns via $0.75/share dividend, $1 billion buybacks.

On capital allocation priorities, with 450,000 BOE per day up 8% YoY and $1.2 billion FCF exceeding guidance by 15%, our framework: fortress balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA 0.7x after $500 million paydown), returns via dividends/buybacks, selective reinvestment. TSR over 120% past 24 months.

Dividends: 12% hike to $0.55 quarterly ($2.20 annual), 17th consecutive, 3.1% yield, 25% FCF payout, 2.0x coverage at $60 WTI/$2.50 gas (breakevens $42 Permian).

Buybacks: $3 billion authorization, $580 million YTD (8.5 million shares at $68 avg), 4-5% EPS accretion. Pause above $85, $2.4 billion remaining.

Reinvestment $2.8 billion capex (flat YoY, 15-20% IRRs): 60% upstream ($1.7 billion)—Permian 22 rigs, costs down 18% to $850/lateral foot, IP30s 1,800 BOE/day; GOM subsalt, Suriname Block 58; 20% midstream ($550 million) Mustang; 20% low-carbon ($550 million) CCUS, blue H2.

50%+ FCF to returns at $70+ oil.

Finally, on debt levels: total gross debt $4.2 billion, down 18% YoY from $5.1 billion on $850 million repayments from $1.2 billion Q3 FCF. Short-term $150 million, long-term $4.05 billion (notes 2026-2033 at 4.2% avg, RCF $2.25 billion drawn 35% of $4.1 billion capacity). 4.5-year WAL.

Net debt $2.85 billion, down 22% YoY, 8% QoQ ($1.35 billion cash). Adjusted $2.4 billion ex-leases. Peers: better than Occidental 1.2x.

Leverage: net debt/LTM EBITDA 0.8x ($3.55 billion EBITDA up 15%), gross 1.2x, debt-to-cap 22%, interest coverage 12.5x, 85% fixed.

Permian monetized $300 million assets; Bakken $150 million cash. Target under $2.5 billion YE 2024, 0.7x at $70 WTI.

I will now turn the call over to Maria Gonzalez for an operational update.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, Alex. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 248,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. Let me provide more detail on these volumes amid WTI at $82 and Henry Hub $2.80.

Total production up 3.3% QoQ from 240,000 BOE/d and 12.7% YoY from 220,000. Oil record 182,000 bbl/d, +7.0% QoQ/+16.2% YoY—Permian 125,000 bbl/d (+10% QoQ) via Mega-Frac (4,500 lbs/ft proppant, 12,000-ft laterals, IP30s 1,800 BOE/d).

Gas equivalent 66,000 BOE/d (396 MMcf/d), -2.4% QoQ but +2.5% YoY on Eagle Ford downtime, Bakken steady 85 MMcf/d.

Permian (65%) 162,000 BOE/d (+5.2% QoQ/+15% YoY), 45 wells WTS, cycle times <90 days. Eagle Ford (20%) 50,000 flat QoQ/+8% YoY, oil cut 65%. Bakken (10%) 28,000 +4% QoQ. GOM (5%) 8,000 steady, VR 341 +1,500 BOE/d.

D&C costs $650/lateral ft (down YoY). Q4 guide 255,000-260,000 BOE/d, oil 185,000-190,000. 10-12% growth 2025.

We also successfully brought new Permian pads online, contributing to growth, and advanced cost reductions.

Now I will turn it over to Robert Hayes for an update on our exploration activities.

Robert Hayes: Thank you, Maria. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Delaware Basin and are planning to drill 12 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio, particularly in Wolfcamp and Bone Springs intervals.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Lisa Chen to discuss our marketing strategy.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Robert. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for our NGL products in the Gulf Coast market area, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen relationships with existing customers. The impact on fractionation spreads and export loadings is significant, generating meaningful incremental revenue.

I will now turn it over to Elena Vasquez to discuss our sustainability efforts.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and operating in a sustainable manner. Before questions, an update on ESG, focusing on emissions reductions. Committed to net-zero Scope 1/2 by 2040, 40% absolute cut by 2030 from 12.5 MtCO2e 2021 baseline. YTD, 22% YoY reduction to 9.8 MtCO2e, intensity 18 kg CO2e/boe (down 25%).

Methane down 35% YoY to 28 kt (0.28%), Luna system on 85% Permian wells, repaired 1,200 points (15 kt). AI predictive like Chevron.

Flaring down 52% to 0.4%, Eagle Ford gathering systems captured 95% gas (+$120 million NGLs). Offshore VRUs <0.2%.

Electrification: Scope 2 down 18%, 65% rigs hybrid wind-solar Bakken/Duvernay; Brazil 50 MW offshore wind cuts diesel 70%.

CCUS: $450 million Jonah facility, 1 MtCO2e/year by 2025, $50-75 million 45Q.

'A' CDP rating, S&P outperforming peers, $2.1 billion green financing at 50 bps savings. $800 million 2024 ESG capex.

Q4 sub-50 barrel spills guide, $200 million capex cathodic/H2 blends.

We are also working to improve water management and protect biodiversity.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss our technology initiatives.

Mike Patel: Thank you, Elena. We are leveraging technology to improve efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance safety. Investments in automation, data analytics, AI optimize operations—like frac scheduling and decline curves. Exploring carbon capture and storage, plus drone LiDAR, DAS for integrity.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Energy Capital Partners. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, and good morning team. Could you walk us through the environmental performance section, particularly spills, incidents, and remediation efforts? We've seen some volatility in peer disclosures post-Permian flaring regulations.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, Sarah. Happy to dive in. At Apex Energy Corp, environmental stewardship is core to our ESG framework, tied to resilience and value. In Q3 2024, we outperformed benchmarks with mature SPCC plans, pipeline integrity, and digital monitoring.

Three reportable spills totaling 42 barrels—68% YoY reduction from 132 barrels across nine in Q3 2023. TTM under 200 barrels, below API <1 bbl/MM produced; at 850,000 BOE/d, rate 0.08 bbl/MM BOE—half peer median IOGP.

Two minor Permian onshore <10 bbl valve releases, one 12-bbl GOM sheen contained by ROV. All secondary containment, no third-party/human factors; TapRooT on infrastructure.

YTD down 72% volume/60% frequency, 18% 5-year CAGR (beats Exxon 14%, Chevron 12%). TRIR 0.12 vs IOGP 0.28.

Permian zero spills ($150 million Integrity 2.0, 4,500 miles pigging, 87 anomalies). GOM down 55% volume AI dashboard. Angola zero with ROV acoustics.

Remediation: 100% contained <4 hours, 96% recovered/bioremediated. Response 17 min avg. 2,500 ft boom, vacuum trucks, bio-gels—no aquifer impact.

Costs $2.8 million, $12 million monitoring in $450 million reserve. No fines, self-reported.

Drone LiDAR 80% Permian pads flags micro-leaks (40% repairs up). SCADA 4.0 predicts 85% failures 72 hrs ahead. Feeds net-zero 2045, methane 0.18%.

Q4 <50 bbls, $200 million capex. De-risks LOE ~5 cents/BOE, first-quartile ESG.

Sarah, does that address, or more regional?

Sarah Jenkins: That's comprehensive—thanks, Alex. Appreciate the Permian details.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Tudor Pickering. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel: Thanks, operator. Good morning, team. Strong quarter—congrats on the beat. Diving into CapEx, can you walk us through the drilling, completion, and facilities breakdown? Budget versus actuals, any color on variances by region, and how that's tying into your returns framework?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Mike—appreciate it. Our YTD Q3 2024 CapEx at $1.8 billion vs $2.0 billion budget, 10% under while hitting production. Reflects discipline at $78 WTI, service deflation 15-20% Permian.

Drilling: Budget $740 million (41%), actual $700 million (39%). 110 gross wells vs 108 planned. 6% under: 12 rigs at $22,000/day, footage 650 ft/day +12% automated. Permian 75% ($525M vs $550M), Eagle Ford 15% ($84M vs $95M), Rockies 10%. Q3 $4.2M/well down from $4.8M.

Completion: Budget $920 million (51%), actual $875 million (49%). 115 wells vs 112. 5% under: stages/day 14.5 +18%, electric fleets cut diesel 40%. Permian 80% ($700M vs $750M), IP30s 1,800 BOE/d. Eagle Ford 12%, Rockies 8%.

Facilities: Budget $340 million (19%), actual $225 million (12%). 34% under modular/tie-backs. Permian water recycling $90M (70% util), Eagle Ford compression $38M, DJ solar $34M. Deferred $60M SWDs.

$135M savings, capital efficiency 85%. 2024 guide $2.4-2.6B, Permian 75%.

Mike, covers it?

Mike Patel: Perfect—thanks, Sarah. Wait, Alex.

Operator: Our next question comes from Brian Walsh with Simmons Energy. Please go ahead.

Brian Walsh: Good morning. What are your expectations for production growth and commodity price realizations into 2025?

Maria Gonzalez: Good morning, Brian. We're guiding 3-5% QoQ growth in Q4 to 255-260k BOE/d, with full-year 2024 up 10-12%. Into 2025, expect 10-12% growth from Permian pads and GOM, funded from cash flow. Realizations hedged 55-65%, oil $74-78, gas $2.90-3.30, resilient to volatility.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Kim with PNC Energy. Please go ahead.

Laura Kim: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Robert Hayes: Thanks, Laura. Our seismic in Delaware confirms high-potential Wolfcamp/Bone Springs prospects. Planning 12 wells next year could add 100-200 MMBoe reserves, shifting strategy toward accelerated development in Tier 1 acreage, boosting inventory to 7+ years and supporting 5% annual growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Reilly with Jefferies. Please go ahead.

Tom Reilly: What is the outlook for the new NGL products in the coming years?

Lisa Chen: Good morning, Tom. Strong Gulf Coast demand, with Mont Belvieu pricing firm. Expect 10-15% volume growth through 2027 on export ramps, enhancing margins 20% YoY, targeting $200 million incremental EBITDA by 2026 via expanded fractionation.

Operator: Our next question comes from Dana Lopez with RBC Capital. Please go ahead.

Dana Lopez: Could you elaborate on your sustainability targets?

Elena Vasquez: Thanks, Dana. On track for 40% Scope 1/2 cut by 2030, YTD 22% ahead. Methane 15-20% intensity drop by 2025 at 0.18% now. CCUS 1 Mt/year 2025, blue H2 500 kt by 2028. Ties to financing KPIs, de-risking access.

Operator: Our next question comes from Chris Evans with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Chris Evans: What are the key technology initiatives you are focused on?

Mike Patel: Good morning, Chris. AI frac design, predictive analytics for leaks, electric fleets, DAS/Drones cutting costs 25-30%. CCUS pilots, ML decline curves improving layering 15%. Drives 20% NPV uplift, 99.98% reliability.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to David Thompson for closing remarks.

David Thompson: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
